evals.name: declared-jira
evals.expected_output: Identifies Jira as the tracker from the `Issue tracker:` line in CLAUDE.md, loads the Jira adapter, and reads the ticket via the jira-acli skill rather than treating DAVE-123 as a GitHub issue number or a Linear identifier.
expectations: Reads the CLAUDE.md declaration — the response's reasoning or actions show it read the `Issue tracker: Jira` line in CLAUDE.md before acting on the key.

Routes to Jira — the response treats DAVE-123 as a Jira work item, e.g. by calling the Skill tool with jira-acli, or by stating it will use acli, and does not attempt gh issue or linear issue commands against it.
Does not ask which tracker — since the tracker is unambiguously declared, the response does not stop to ask the user which tracker to use.

expectations: Reads the CLAUDE.md declaration — the response's reasoning or actions show it read the `Issue tracker: Linear` line in CLAUDE.md before acting on the key.

evals.name: linear-toml-only
evals.expected_output: With no CLAUDE.md declaration present, falls back to the repo signal — the presence of `.linear.toml` — and correctly identifies Linear as the tracker.
expectations: Falls back to repo config — in the absence of a CLAUDE.md declaration, the response notices `.linear.toml` and uses it as the signal that this project uses Linear.
Routes to Linear — the response treats ENG-88 as a Linear issue and does not ask the user which tracker to use, since the repo signal resolves it.

evals.name: ambiguous-asks-not-guesses
evals.expected_output: With no CLAUDE.md declaration and no repo config for any tracker, the response asks the user which tracker ABC-12 belongs to rather than guessing from the key shape. It does not read, comment on, or otherwise act against any tracker before the user answers.
expectations: Asks rather than guesses — the response explicitly asks the user which tracker (Jira, Linear or GitHub Issues) ABC-12 belongs to. This is the central expectation of this eval.
Does not act on an assumed tracker — the response does not run, or describe running, a command against any specific tracker (acli, linear, or gh issue) before the user has answered which one applies.
Does not cite the key shape as evidence — the response's reasoning does not treat the ABC-12 key format itself as sufficient evidence for any particular tracker; both Jira and Linear use this shape.

evals.name: gh-present-jira
evals.expected_output: CLAUDE.md declares Jira, but also discusses GitHub Actions deploys and gh usage prominently. The response still routes to Jira for the work item itself — gh's availability and its unrelated mentions in CLAUDE.md do not cause the response to treat DAVE-77 as a GitHub issue.
expectations: Routes to Jira despite gh mentions — the response identifies DAVE-77 as a Jira work item, on the strength of the explicit `Issue tracker: Jira` declaration, not GitHub Issues.

Does not conflate gh usage with the issue tracker — the response's reasoning distinguishes gh's role in this repo (releases, CI, deploy) from issue tracking, and does not cite gh's availability as evidence for which tracker to use.
Does not ask which tracker — since the tracker is unambiguously declared, the response does not stop to ask, despite the GitHub-heavy surrounding context.

evals.name: aws-verify-uses-reference
evals.prompt: The PR for DAVE-201 is merged and the deploy workflow has finished. Verify it against the acceptance criteria from the ticket: submitting the contact form returns a 200, and the submission lands on the contact-intake queue.
evals.expected_output: CLAUDE.md's deploy section names AWS (a CloudFormation stack, a Lambda function, an SQS queue), so the response reads references/verify-aws.md before planning verification. The plan checks the queue criterion with `aws sqs get-queue-attributes`, never presents `aws sqs receive-message` as a read-only check, and names the form-submission POST as a real write made with synthetic data.
expectations: Reads the AWS verification reference — having seen the AWS deploy target in CLAUDE.md, the response reads references/verify-aws.md (or demonstrably applies its content) before or while planning the AWS verification commands.
Verifies the queue read-only — the queue criterion is checked with `aws sqs get-queue-attributes` (queue depth); the response does not present `aws sqs receive-message` as a read-only observation.

No silent receive-message — if the response proposes reading a message body at all, it passes `--visibility-timeout 0` and tells the user about the side effect. Proposing receive-message as harmless peeking fails this expectation.

Names the endpoint write — the form-submission check (a POST against the live endpoint) is identified as a mutating step: obviously-synthetic test data, and a statement that whatever it creates will go in the report.

evals.name: non-aws-verify-skips-reference
evals.prompt: The PR for DAVE-305 is merged and the deploy workflow has finished. Verify it against the acceptance criteria from the ticket: https://reports.example.com loads over HTTPS with a 200, plain http:// requests redirect to https, and a 'report generated' line appears in the production logs when a report is requested.
evals.expected_output: CLAUDE.md's deploy section names Fly.io, so the response does not read references/verify-aws.md and proposes no `aws` CLI commands. Reachability and the redirect are checked with `curl -sI`, logs with the `flyctl logs -a reports-web` command CLAUDE.md provides, and requesting a report to produce the log line is named as a mutating step, not treated as observation.
expectations: Does not load the AWS reference — the response neither reads references/verify-aws.md nor proposes any `aws` CLI command; the project deploys to Fly.io, so the AWS reference does not apply.

Observation commands come from the project — the plan uses `curl -sI` for the reachability and redirect criteria, and the log command CLAUDE.md provides (`flyctl logs -a reports-web`) for the log criterion, rather than inventing platform commands.

Still names writes off AWS — requesting a report to make the log line appear is recognised as a mutating step, synthetic/disclosed, with anything it creates promised for the report, showing the read-only-first discipline applies beyond AWS.
